title: HAWK-I instrument spies a super galaxy
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 157, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 157 · constellation Cetus · about 75 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A sweep of stars through the middle of NGC 157 traces a giant letter S, a shape that reminds the source of Superman's emblem. This spiral galaxy lies about 75 million light-years away in the constellation Cetus, the Sea Monster.

The picture was taken with HAWK-I, the High-Acuity Wide-field K-band Imager, on ESO's Very Large Telescope at Paranal Observatory in Chile. HAWK-I detects infrared light, which passes through the gas and dust that usually block our view. That lets astronomers look into dense regions where stars are forming, which would otherwise stay hidden.

Star formation matters for our own story too. The processes now gathering material together and making stars in NGC 157 also worked in the Milky Way around 4.5 billion years ago, when they formed the Sun. Studying them in another galaxy is a way of learning where we came from.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (5.67 x 5.67 arcminutes) and distance (75 million light years), the frame spans roughly 124,000 × 124,000 light-years. Its light set out about 75 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: HAWK-I on the Very Large Telescope observed NGC 157 in near-infrared light through Y, H and K filters. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Infrared light is invisible to the eye, so the colours here are a translation of light no one could see directly.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: NGC 157 is faint, at about magnitude 11, yet dedicated amateur astronomers can still track it down with their own telescopes. When the image was released, HAWK-I was described as one of the newest and most powerful instruments on the VLT.
alt: A spiral galaxy whose central band of stars curves into an S shape.
